paper.title: Using protein-per-mRNA differences among human tissues in codon optimization

generators.name: probabilistic tissue codon generator
generators.description: Generate synonymous coding sequences by selecting codons with probabilities proportional to tissue-specific importance weights.

evidence.quote: Therefore, for each amino acid, a certain codon is selected with a probability proportional to the first. If the selected codon is enriched in the tissue, it is incorporated into the sequence.

constraints.name: tissue codon optimization
constraints.description: Maximize codon usage aligned with lung tissue PTR-derived codon preferences.

evidence.quote: We then use these identified patterns for the development of CUSTOM, a codon optimizer algorithm which suggests a synonymous codon design in order to optimize protein production in a tissue-specific manner.

constraints.name: GC content target
constraints.description: Keep GC content near the desired target for mRNA stability.

evidence.quote: GC content: a measure of similarity between the sequence GC content and a desired target value of GC

constraints.name: homopolymer filter
constraints.description: Filter sequences with homopolymers at or above length 7 that impede expression.

evidence.quote: Homopolymers: filters out sequences with homopolymers of a certain length, which can lead to worse expression
Sequences with homopolymers equal or larger than 7 were filtered out and scored

optimizers.name: pool propose-score-select
optimizers.description: Generate a pool of tissue-optimized sequences and select the top-scoring candidate.

evidence.quote: We follow a simple probabilistic approach with two steps: (1) translate tissue-specific codon preferences into a pool of optimal sequences and (2) select the desired sequence based on other parameters of relevance.
Sequences were optimized to either lung or kidney, generating a total of n_pool = 1000.
CUSTOM is publicly available as a Python package (https://github.com/hexavier/CUSTOM) and as a web interface (https://custom.crg.eu).
Once a pool of optimized sequences has been generated, the best-ranked ones can be selected as the user desires.

steps.operation: score tissue codon usage, GC content, and composite metrics

evidence.quote: Among the top 10 scoring candidates of each optimization, we selected 2x eGFPKidney, 2x eGFPLung
We applied CUSTOM to the protein sequences of eGFP and mCherry (Uniprot ID: C5MKY7, X5DSL3). Sequences were optimized to either lung or kidney

assumptions: eGFP CDS length (~720 bp) stands in for the full coding sequence optimized in the paper.
Pool MCMC with n_pool=500 approximates CUSTOM n_pool=1000 at reduced cost while staying minute-scale.
Tissue codon weights are a simplified static profile rather than the full random-forest PTR model.
MFE, CAI, CPB, and ENC scoring from select_best are deferred; tissue codon + GC + homopolymer gate the v1 baseline.
unknowns: ViennaRNA MFE scoring is not bound in v1 Proto baseline.
Exact CUSTOM random-forest tissue feature weights are not reproduced.
Bidirectional TRE3G cloning context from expression vector design is not modeled.
